From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Subject: POC call recap & next steps

Hi Sofia / Jin —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment heading into the POC: 

1) Objectives / success criteria (as discussed):
   - Reduce average latency for search-ranking completions to < 350ms 95th percentile.
   - Maintain answer relevance at or above current baseline (ACME internal eval) — target precision@5 >= 0.78.
   - Support English + Spanish customer queries for the initial trial.

2) Trial scope & timeline:
   - 4-week POC starting Jun 7 — week 0 is integration + data onboarding, weeks 1-3 evaluation.
   - Redwood will provide a sandbox API key + model variants and a shared evaluation harness (Drive link attached).

3) Model selection (initial recommendation):
   - Primary: Mistral-7B-instruct (open, strong English baseline; fast inference profile).
   - Fallback / multilingual: Llama-2-13B-chat-qa (quantized variant) for Spanish fallback — slower but stronger multilingual capability.
   - We'll provide both and an automated fallback routing policy for Spanish-heavy queries.

4) Ownership & contacts:
   - ACME: Sofia Ramos (product) + Jin Park (engineering).
   - Redwood: Ben Carter (deal owner), Marissa Cole (solutions / model selection), Laura Bennett (CS engineering).

5) Next steps (action items):
   - Redwood: share POC plan + sample eval prompts and access (Ben) — by May 22.
   - ACME: provide sample query logs and a short prioritized prompt set (Sofia) — by May 28.
   - Schedule 30m kickoff for integration week — suggested Jun 7 10am PT. Jordan will send invite.

Attachments: Acme_POCTemplate.pdf (POC checklist), redwood-model-recommendation.xlsx (model perf notes).

If anything above needs correction, flag now — otherwise we'll proceed with the timeline above.

Thanks,
Ben

Subject: Re: POC call recap & next steps

Thanks Ben — a couple of technical clarifications from the solutions side to make the model recommendations actionable: 

- For Mistral-7B-instruct we'll provide a 4-bit quantized variant optimized for latency on our hosted Dedicated pools. It hits the throughput targets in our benchmarks for short completion lengths (<= 128 tokens).

- For Spanish support, the Llama-2-13B-chat-qa quantized model provides better translation/QA behavior out of the box. If ACME expects heavy Spanish traffic (> 30% of queries), we should plan to run a small calibration dataset through both models in week 0 to see the precision tradeoffs.

- Evaluation harness: we'll include the following metrics in the Drive folder: latency p50/p95, tokens-per-second, precision@k (k=1,5), and a small human-eval rubric for ambiguous cases.

- Feature flags / routing: We'll set up a language-detection routing rule that sends Spanish-labeled queries to the 13B fallback. We can switch to a confidence-based fallback after the calibration run.

I'll attach a short checklist of what we need from ACME for week 0: sample logs (anonymized), a prioritized prompt list for both English and Spanish, and one canonical evaluation dashboard user.

Marissa
